description: Receive e-prescriptions, faxed, and phoned prescriptions; data entry; DUR and allergy checks; pharmacist verification; labels; filling
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patient safety: profiles, allergies, and DUR alerts live only in the PMS; about 55 prescriptions and $3,600 of sales per business day; patients who are turned away for a day often transfer for good
source_evidence: EV-050 (pharmacist-owner interview); EV-044 (sales per business day); EV-045 (prescription volume)
manual_workaround: Downtime procedure: emergency refills of up to a 72-hour supply from the patient's labeled bottle when the prescriber cannot be reached (Fla. Stat. 465.0275(1)); transfer urgent new prescriptions to the partner pharmacy; paper downtime log for back-entry
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; e-prescribing network (through the PMS vendor); internet provider; MSP
dependent_people_or_facilities: Pharmacist-owner; Staff Pharmacist; both technicians; prescription department

business_process: Controlled substance dispensing and DEA and Florida duties
description: Receive and process EPCS; consult the PDMP before dispensing; nightly PDMP report; review the daily EPCS audit report; keep controlled substance records
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: EPCS may be processed only in the audited pharmacy application and its records kept electronically (21 CFR 1311.200(a); 1311.305(a)); PDMP report due by the close of the next business day (Fla. Stat. 893.055(3)(a)); if the PDMP cannot be reached because of a technical failure, the reason is documented and no more than a 3-day supply may be dispensed (893.055(8))
source_evidence: EV-050 (pharmacist-owner interview); EV-005 (nightly PDMP file); EV-045 (controlled substance share)
manual_workaround: PDMP web portal from a clean device; document any PDMP outage and limit to a 3-day supply; EPCS cannot be processed outside the PMS, so ask prescribers to re-send them after recovery or to send urgent ones to the partner pharmacy; paper controlled substance log for back-entry
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; e-prescribing network; Florida PDMP

description: Real-time claims to PBMs through the claims switch; copay collection; rejection handling; reconciliation of PBM payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without adjudication the pharmacy cannot price prescriptions or collect copays; PBM remittances fund the weekly wholesaler payment; cash reserve about 3 weeks
source_evidence: EV-050 (Lead Pharmacy Technician interview); EV-044 (cash reserve; weekly wholesaler payment)
manual_workaround: Dispense urgent prescriptions and record them on the downtime log; collect copays when claims are submitted after recovery; call PBM help desks for urgent coverage questions
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; claims switch (through the PMS vendor); PBMs; internet provider

description: Hand out filled prescriptions; capture pickup signatures; pharmacist counseling; front-store register
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Filled prescriptions waiting in bins are useless if staff cannot confirm the patient and the price; most patients come the same day they are notified
source_evidence: EV-050 (Staff Pharmacist interview); EV-047 (standalone card terminal)
manual_workaround: Paper pickup log with signatures; filled bags carry printed labels; the card terminal is standalone and keeps working; counsel from the printed label and monograph
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-03 (pickup counter station and signature pad); SYS-04
dependent_people_or_facilities: Front-Store Clerk; Staff Pharmacist; pickup counter

business_process: Adherence packaging for ALF residents and home patients
description: Weekly multi-dose strip packs for about 70 patients (about 40 ALF residents); orders flow from the PMS to the packaging workstation; packs checked by a pharmacist and delivered on Wednesdays
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Packs are built 2 days before the Wednesday delivery, which gives about 48 hours of slack; ALF residents miss doses if packs are late; the ALF management company can move its business
source_evidence: EV-050 (Lead Pharmacy Technician interview); EV-045 (adherence pack volume); EV-018 (SYS-05 image backup)
manual_workaround: Hand-filled blister cards or labeled vials checked by a pharmacist; notify ALF nurses of the change; prioritize ALF residents over home patients
dependent_systems: SYS-05; SYS-01; SYS-07 (image backup of the SYS-05 workstation)
dependent_third_parties: Packaging equipment vendor; PMS vendor; MSP; ALF management company
dependent_people_or_facilities: Lead Pharmacy Technician; pharmacists; packaging room

description: About 25 deliveries a day to homes and the two ALFs; proof of delivery captured in the app
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Homebound patients depend on delivery; a one-day delay is tolerable if urgent items are prioritized
source_evidence: EV-050 (Store Manager interview); EV-045 (deliveries a day); EV-009 (delivery app)
manual_workaround: Printed route sheet and paper signature slips; pharmacist calls patients with urgent items

description: Refill phone line and text reminders (in the PMS); store phones; faxes with prescribers; email with the ALFs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Patients and prescribers must reach the pharmacy about urgent refills and authorizations; faxes queue at the vendor
manual_workaround: Forward the main line to the pharmacist-owner's cell phone; ask prescribers to re-send; read faxes in the vendor web portal from a clean device
dependent_systems: SYS-01 (refill line); SYS-02; SYS-04 (VoIP phones); SYS-06
dependent_third_parties: PMS vendor; phone carrier; cloud fax vendor; productivity suite vendor

description: Daily orders on the wholesaler portal; Schedule II orders with the CSOS certificate; receiving; controlled substance inventory
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Next-day delivery from the wholesaler; about 2 days of stock on hand for fast movers; Schedule II orders need a CSOS signature or a paper DEA order form
manual_workaround: Phone orders to the wholesaler sales representative; paper DEA order forms for Schedule II; borrow stock from the partner pharmacy
dependent_systems: Wholesaler ordering portal (no ePHI); SYS-03 (owner laptop with the CSOS certificate)

description: Shared-drive documents (ALF order sheets, packaging schedules, controlled substance inventory spreadsheets, delivery logs, HR files); payroll through the payroll service; bookkeeping
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Biweekly payroll; the ALF order sheets are also in the PMS and the fax portal, so the shared drive is not the only copy
source_evidence: EV-050 (Store Manager interview); EV-001 (payroll schedule); EV-018 (backup schedule)
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll through the payroll service; ask the ALFs to re-send order sheets
dependent_third_parties: Productivity suite vendor; backup service (MSP subcontractor); MSP; payroll service
